alert.label: from the collapse to the mass SMS alert (679,295 messages)

rasuwa.label: for the wave to reach the Rasuwagadhi gauge; its last reading was 27% of its warning level, then it went silent

syabru.label: to reach Syabrubesi: 16 to 26 minutes before the alert

passes.label: NISAR ascending pairs over the source before the collapse; 4 were public on ASF before it, 3 were processed later

story.morning: At 08:37:10 Nepal time a combined ice and bedrock mass broke away high on the Langtang massif; UNOSAT mapped the detachment zone at 1.96 km². The flood ran down the Bhote Koshi and the Trishuli. Nepal's operational log first recorded it as an M4.4 earthquake.
story.morning2: The three gauges nearest the source were destroyed before any of them crossed its warning level: their last readings were 27%, 69% and 87% of warning. Gauges further down survived and recorded the flood. Radar had watched the slope all summer, but it was one of 193 moving patches in the box, with no rule to pick it out.
story.creep: In the 24 days ending 7 days before the collapse (26 Jul → 19 Aug), the fastest tenth of the detachment zone moved 1.02 m downhill; the zone's median moved 0.05 m. Meena 2026 reports 0.96 m for the same pass, as the median over the crown, a smaller area, so it checks the size of the motion, not the exact number. It moved 0.95 m in 20 Jun → 2 Jul too, so the motion did not single out the last weeks. In 14 Jul → 26 Jul no moving patch formed within 2 km of the source. That pass had the noisiest offsets of the summer: the 3σ cut was 0.74 m, above the 0.50 m that the fastest tenth of the detachment zone moved. Phase coherence at the site was the best of the 7 passes, but no phase motion there passed the ±50 mm threshold.

limits: The pre-registered test fails: the source valley ranked #2 in the last pass but was not ranked one pass earlier. In 14 Jul → 26 Jul no moving patch formed within 2 km of the source. That pass had the noisiest offsets of the summer: the 3σ cut was 0.74 m, above the 0.50 m that the fastest tenth of the detachment zone moved. Phase coherence at the site was the best of the 7 passes, but no phase motion there passed the ±50 mm threshold.

The screen keeps this valley near the top most of the summer (6 of 7 ascending passes in the top 5) and after the collapse too (#10, #3, #22, #7, #1). It says 'watch this valley', not 'it falls next week'.
Only 4 of those 7 pairs were public on ASF before the collapse; 3 (15 May→27 May, 27 May→8 Jun, 8 Jun→20 Jun) were processed afterwards. The last pass went public 37 hours before the collapse.

Backtest, with the same rules: on the Budhi Gandaki rock avalanche (Oct 2026) the source ranked #10 then not ranked, so the test fails there too. False alarms (another valley in the top 5 in two passes in a row): Budhi Gandaki 5 in 11 passes, Manang (no failure) 3 in 8 passes, Langtang 4 in 7 passes.

Judged by the zone a valley sensor could watch rather than the exact slope (5 km, same drainage, top 10: chosen after seeing these results), Budhi Gandaki was on the list in 2 of its last two passes and in 7 of 11 passes against 3.6 expected by chance (p = 0.026). That scale is now fixed in advance as rule v2 for the next events.
The rules were written after the event, by people who had read post-event studies of it. Pre-registration only guards against tuning on our own results.
Phase patches carry millimetre uncertainties (the bootstrap error of the patch mean, which shrinks with patch size), so large phase patches dominate a score of motion over noise.

The headline phase is not corrected for tropospheric delay, which at 5,510 m can mimic motion. A sensitivity run that subtracts each product's own wet and hydrostatic screens gives #2 in the last pass and still not ranked one pass earlier.
The hit zone is 2 km around a 2.0 km² outline, so several patches qualify in most passes, and the one that counts changes from pass to pass.
The USGS source point sits 1.3 km outside the UNOSAT outline; the outline is used as truth, as pre-registered. The flow path and the same-channel test start at the USGS point.
NISAR L2 products are provisional, one track per direction, and there is no earlier-year NISAR archive to separate seasonal snow change from precursor motion.
Arrival times between gauges are interpolated along the routed flow path and differ from some reported times (Timure); beyond Betrawati they are extrapolated.
ERA5 is a 0.25° grid cell at 5,510 m. The temperature anomaly is stable across elevations; the snowfall figure is not (7% of normal here, 1.5% at 5,190 m).

A few implementation constants live in code, not in config.json: the 30% glacier fraction for ice over rock, the 10 mm gate for opposing neighbours, the season mapping 1 + 0.25·z (clipped 0.5–1.5) from 1 May, and the 30% valid-share and 20° stable-ground cuts.
The Sentinel-1 C-band control is not run yet; it needs the ASF HyP3 service authorised on the Earthdata account.
real: 20 NISAR L2 GUNW + GOFF pairs (ascending track 98, descending track 48), read from ASF, box subset only.
NISAR GCOV backscatter for 4 ascending dates; the change map between 19 Aug and 31 Aug shows the avalanche path through monsoon cloud.
Detachment zone, flood extent, affected buildings and roads: UNOSAT product 4257.
Gauge series and the alert chronology: DHM river watch via the Acharya & Paudel archive (Zenodo 22679444); USGS and GEOFON catalogues.
Terrain: Copernicus DEM GLO-30. Glaciers: RGI 7.0. People: WorldPop 2026. Rivers and places: OpenStreetMap. Heat: ERA5 via Open-Meteo.
method_html:
Method

One question, answered with a number: with rules fixed in advance, would NISAR have put the Langtang valley on a watch list a week before it fell? The unit is a valley, not a pixel.

1 · Fetch

NISAR L2 GUNW (unwrapped phase, coherence, offsets, LOS geometry) and GOFF (dense pixel offsets, three window sizes, with variances) for every pair from 15 May to 18 Oct 2026, and GCOV backscatter for key dates. Only the 463×412 cell box (80 m, UTM 45N) is read from each granule. Where two releases exist we use P05023, the composite that was on ASF before the collapse; 3 of the 7 ascending pre-collapse pairs exist only as X05026, processed after it.

2 · Clean

  • Offsets: cull by variance (σ ≤ 1 m), SNR ≥ 5 and a 5×5 median test; remove the bulk shift; project slant-range and along-track offsets onto the local fall line from the DEM, weighted by their variances. The GOFF layer with the lowest noise over stable ground is used per pass. Glaciers come out moving downhill, which checks the sign conventions.
  • Phase: subtract the ionosphere screen, convert with the product's own wavelength (λ = 0.2420, 0.2439 m), keep coherence ≥ 0.3 (ascending) or 0.4 (descending) and valid connected components, remove a robust plane and the median of a 3–5 km ring.

3 · Rank

Patches are connected groups (≥ 5 cells) of downhill offset motion above 3× the scene noise with direction coherence above the scene median, or of relative LOS motion beyond ±50 mm. Each patch gets a bootstrap σ, direction coherence, an opposing-neighbour flag (within 1.5 km), an ice-over-rock flag (glacier ≥ 30% and slope ≥ 30°), WorldPop residents within 1 km of its first 30 km downstream (D8 routing on the DEM) and the ERA5 heat anomaly. Score = (motion/sigma) * dir_coherence * (opposing_bonus if opposing_sign) * (ice_bonus if ice_over_rock) * (1 + w_pop*log10(1+people_below)) * (1 + w_season*(season_anomaly-1)), with opposing bonus 1.5, ice bonus 1.3, w_pop 0.25, w_season 0.5.

4 · Score against truth

A hit is the best-ranked patch within 2 km of the UNOSAT detachment outline whose flow path joins the source's before the main river. Truth is never used to rank. Pass condition, fixed before the first run: a blob within 2 km of the source and in the same catchment ranks top 5 in BOTH of the last two ascending windows before 26 Aug. Baseline: rank by mean raw offset magnitude alone.

5 · Replay

The flood front runs down the D8 flow path through the DHM gauge brackets. The tripwire fires only if the source valley was in the top N of the last pass; its delay is the sum of the four sliders.

The thresholds and weights above are in pipeline/config.json, committed before the first results (see Data, and the git history). A few implementation constants live in rank.py and clean.py; they are listed under Limits. The browser scorer is tested to reproduce the pipeline ranking exactly.

Data

  • NISAR L2 GUNW, GOFF and GCOV, provisional (NASA/JPL/ISRO), via ASF DAAC and NASA Earthdata (collection NISAR_L2_GUNW_PROVISIONAL_V1).
  • UNOSAT product 4257: detachment zone (Landsat 9, 26 Aug 2026), flood extent, affected buildings and roads, barrier lakes.
  • Copernicus EMS rapid mapping EMSR927.
  • Nepal Department of Hydrology and Meteorology river-watch ten-minute stage series, as archived by Acharya & Paudel (Zenodo 22679444).
  • USGS earthquake catalogue (us7000tbwb, us7000tc90); GEOFON (gfz2026qrfy).
  • Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA, AWS open data); GLIMS/RGI glacier outlines; WorldPop population; OpenStreetMap (ODbL); ERA5 reanalysis via Open-Meteo.

Papers

  • Kutoğlu, Softa & Akgün (2026). Remote Sensing 18(21), 3727 (NISAR observations of differential rock–ice deformation before the Langtang cascade).
  • Meena (2026). NISAR offsets measure pre-failure motion but do not single out the Bhote Koshi avalanche source. Research Square.
  • Acharya (2026). The Bhote Koshi–Trishuli flash flood of 26 August 2026: warning latency exceeded flood travel time. EarthArXiv 14687, v5.
  • Hassan et al. (2026). Extreme heat and snow drought preconditioned the August 2026 Nepal rock–ice avalanche flood. Research Square.
  • Sah (2026). Sentinel-1 analysis of the source slope, code and data release: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22676918.

sah.text: Sah (2026) tested routine Sentinel-1 products at this slope and found no motion above 12.8 mm a month (48-day pairs).

why_missing: In 14 Jul → 26 Jul no moving patch formed within 2 km of the source. That pass had the noisiest offsets of the summer: the 3σ cut was 0.74 m, above the 0.50 m that the fastest tenth of the detachment zone moved. Phase coherence at the site was the best of the 7 passes, but no phase motion there passed the ±50 mm threshold.

rule_evidence.text: Standard radar practice: only motion that clears the measurement noise counts (here 3× the scene noise for offsets, ±50 mm for phase).
Meena 2026 found the source moved consistently downslope: directional coherence 0.87 at the crown against 0.69 for the surrounding box.
Kutoğlu et al. 2026 report differential rock–ice deformation before the collapse: a +63 mm line-of-sight cluster 1.4 km from the detachment, beside a -71 mm feature.
The source was a combined ice and bedrock mass (Acharya & Paudel 2026). Steep glacier-covered rock is where ice–rock avalanches start.
Risk is hazard times exposure: WorldPop residents within reach of the routed flow path.
Hassan et al. 2026: the July–August heat anomaly reached about the 98th percentile of 1979–2025, with a snowfall deficit, before the failure.

sensitivity.note: Same pipeline, but each GUNW's wet + hydrostatic tropospheric phase screens are subtracted before ranking. Headline keeps the pre-registered processing.

pass_with_tropo.rule: a blob within 2 km of the source and in the same catchment ranks top 5 in BOTH of the last two ascending windows before 26 Aug
